name: Introduction to Ethics in Research
description:
The Institute Ethics Committee (IEC) reviews research proposals to evaluate risks associated with research that involves human participants. The process follows national guidelines for research ethics, and this course is intended to familiarize the students with the process of obtaining ethics approval for their proposed research. As a part of this course, the students will learn about the process of applying for ethics approval for research proposal, and process of evaluation of responsible research that is in aligned with current national guidelines. 
Session 1: Introduction to the Institute Ethics Committee 
Session 2: Objectives and operating principles for ethics involving human research 
Session 3: Committee composition, membership and roles & function
Session 4: Types of research proposals and guidelines for application to approval
Session 5: Types of research proposals and guidelines for application to approval
Session 6: Familiarity with the review process 
Session 7: Guidelines for informed consent, Participant Information Sheet 
Session 8: Guidelines for vulnerable population, inclusion-exclusion criterion
Session 9: Guidelines for vulnerable population, inclusion-exclusion criterion
Session 10: Guidelines for conflict of interest, compensation
Session 11: Guidelines for research involving national, international collaboration
Session 12: Guidelines for social sciences, non-medical research
Session 13: Special topics
Session 14: Special topics
